# SPE Round r01 Plan: triage agent

Defaults I chose for missing details. The 40 tickets and the support lead's labels are at `data/eval/tickets.jsonl` and `data/eval/labels.jsonl`. If they live somewhere else, I will move them there in step 1. Exact model IDs and prices get checked against current Anthropic docs in step 1, before the prediction is saved.

## 0. Setup (after approval)

1. Create `spe/` with the layout from the SPE way. Save your prompt and any planning answers word for word to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`.
3. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` from section 2. Its first line reads `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` Its author is "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode". It has `same_as_last_round: null` because this is round 1.
4. Commit `SPE r01 specify` and then `SPE r01 predict: baseline vs few-shot vs small model`. All commits stay local. I will not push.

## 1. Specify

### Requirements (`spe/spec/spec.md`, round r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns exactly one category from billing, bug, how-to, account, outage. | User: "triage tickets" | Code: the output enum is valid and matches the reference label |
| R2 | The agent assigns exactly one priority from P1 to P4. | User: "triage tickets" | Code: the output enum is valid and matches the reference label |
| R3 | Category accuracy is at least 0.85 on the 40 tickets. | Default D1 for "correctly" | Code: exact match rate |
| R4 | Priority is within one level of the reference on at least 0.90 of tickets. | Default D1 for "correctly" | Code: abs(pred minus ref) is at most 1 |
| R5 | The agent flags every reference P1 ticket as P1. | Default D2. A missed outage costs the most. | Code: recall on reference P1 tickets |
| R6 | The agent drafts a first reply that answers the ticket, invents no facts, makes no refund or ETA promises, and asks for missing info when needed. | User: "drafts a first reply" (project brief) | Judge: 4-check rubric, pass means all 4 pass |
| R7 | Output is valid JSON with `category`, `priority`, `reply`, `reason`. | Decision: needed for code grading | Code: schema validation |
| R8 | Mean cost is at most $0.010 per ticket. | Default D3 for "cheaply" | Code: API token usage times the price table |
| R9 | The agent sees only the ticket text. It never sees labels, graders, or predictions. | SPE way | Code: input audit and a transcript scan for label paths and label strings |

No proposals exist from an earlier round, so nothing is adopted or rejected yet.

### Disagreements and defaults (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Question | Default used in r01 | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What counts as "correct"? | Category 0.85, priority within one level 0.90 | User |
| D2 | Must P1 recall be 1.0? | Yes, it is a hard target | User or support lead |
| D3 | What counts as "cheap"? | $0.010 per ticket or less | User |
| D4 | Do the 40 tickets contain customer PII that should not go to the API? | I assume they are cleared for API use. I will halt if I see raw card numbers or passwords. | User |
| D5 | Is one support lead's priority call the ground truth? | Yes for r01. Priority disagreements get logged as possible label noise, not fixed. | Support lead |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations (one change each)

| Config | What it is | The one change |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Naive code baseline. It always answers the most common reference category and P3. It writes no reply. | Reference point only. It costs $0. |
| C1 | Default mid-tier Claude model (Sonnet tier), zero-shot prompt with category and priority definitions, JSON output. | Baseline |
| C2 | C1 plus 6 few-shot examples that I write from the definitions. No eval ticket is used as an example. | Adds few-shot examples |
| C3 | C1 on the small model tier (Haiku tier). | Swaps the model |

### Prediction table

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. Each cell is the mean over 3 trials per ticket.

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | C3 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | 0.30 ± 0.10 | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | 0.78 ± 0.08 | Code: exact match | Five categories are distinct, but billing vs account and bug vs outage overlap. |
| Priority exact match | 0.35 ± 0.10 | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.65 ± 0.10 | 0.52 ± 0.10 | Code: exact match | Priority is a judgment call, and one person set the labels. |
| Priority within one level | 0.80 ± 0.10 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.93 ± 0.05 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | Code: abs diff at most 1 | Most misses will be off by one level, not two. |
| P1 recall | 0.00 ± 0.00 | 0.85 ± 0.15 | 0.90 ± 0.10 | 0.75 ± 0.20 | Code: recall on reference P1 | Outages read as urgent, but a calmly written P1 will be missed. The band is wide because the set likely holds only 4 to 6 P1 tickets. |
| Schema valid rate | 1.00 ± 0.00 | 1.00 ± 0.01 | 1.00 ± 0.01 | 0.99 ± 0.02 | Code: JSON schema | Structured output makes invalid JSON rare. |
| Reply pass rate | 0.00 ± 0.00 | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.72 ± 0.10 | Judge: 4-check rubric | The small model will invent fixes or ETAs more often. Few-shot examples do not change replies much. |
| Cost per ticket (USD) | 0.000 ± 0.000 | 0.008 ± 0.004 | 0.011 ± 0.005 | 0.003 ± 0.002 | Code: usage times prices | About 1,500 input and 400 output tokens. C2 adds about 1,200 input tokens. |

Overall prediction: C2 meets R3 and R4 but fails R8 by a small margin. C1 is the best fit for "correctly and cheaply". C3 is cheapest but fails R3, R5, and R6. No config reaches P1 recall of 1.0 in r01.

## 3. Evaluate

### Build (before the harness)

1. Write `triage/prompt.md`, `triage/schema.json`, and `triage/run.ts`. The runner takes a config name and one ticket's text and returns the JSON output plus token usage.
2. Write `triage/fewshot.md` for C2 from the category and priority definitions only.

### Harness (`spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`)

1. `const ROUND = "r01"`. Every path and prompt reads the round from this constant.
2. Graders live in `spe/evals/graders/`. Code checks run first. The judge runs only for R6. The judge sees the ticket and the reply. It does not see the config name or the reference label.
3. Gate 1, grader selftest. The oracle (reference labels plus a hand-written good reply) passes. An empty output fails. A wrong output with shifted labels fails. The run stops if any of these behave otherwise.
4. Gate 2, control regrade. Round 1 has no earlier round, so this gate does not apply. I log that as a default.
5. Gate 3, dry run. I run C1 and C3 on 3 tickets each and check that the schema, cost logging, and the transcript scan all work.
6. Full run: 40 tickets times 3 configs (C1 to C3) times 3 trials is 360 agent calls. C0 is computed in code.
7. Leak scan. Any trial whose transcript contains a label file path or a reference label field gets voided and logged.
8. Split cells. A ticket where the 3 trials disagree on category or priority gets up to 2 extra trials. The total cap is 120 extra trials.
9. Cost cap. The run stops starting new trials at $15 total spend. Any skipped trial gets logged.
10. Failure analysis. It groups misses into F-numbered types such as "billing read as account" or "calm P1 rated P3".
11. Completeness critic. A separate agent checks that every prediction cell has a measured value and every void or skip is explained.

### Workflow arguments

```
ROUND: "r01"
configs: ["C1", "C2", "C3"]
tickets: "data/eval/tickets.jsonl"
labels: "data/eval/labels.jsonl"   # grader only
trials_per_cell: 3
extra_trials_cap: 120
budget_usd: 15
concurrency: 4
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

I expect 360 agent calls, up to 120 extra calls, and one judge call per reply. The estimate is $3 to $8 in total. The $15 cap is the hard limit.

### Commits

1. `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)` after the gates pass.
2. `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>` when the Workflow completion notice arrives.

## 4. Learn (after the completion notice)

1. Write `spe/prediction-log.md` with one row per cell: Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, Closer. Under it, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. I will state plainly whether the C0 naive baseline beat any prediction.
2. Write `spe/failures.md` with each new F type. Each entry lists name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure, with original and regraded numbers side by side.
3. Add "Proposed for round r02" to the spec and write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
4. Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r01` locally.

## Halt conditions

I will stop and report if the budget cap is hit, a label leaks into a trial, a grader fails its selftest, or D4 turns out to block API use of the tickets.
critiques: Section 1 turns 'triage tickets correctly and cheaply' into requirements R1 to R9. Each row has a Source and a Test column, such as 'Code: exact match rate' for R3 and 'Judge: 4-check rubric' for R6. Vague words like 'correctly' and 'cheaply' become defaults D1 and D3, and both are logged in disagreements.md.

The prediction table gives a number and a band for every metric under every config C0 to C3. Examples are 'Category accuracy 0.85 ± 0.07' for C1 and 'Cost per ticket 0.003 ± 0.002' for C3. It uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Every metric row has a 'Why' column. Some rows explain the gaps between configs, such as reply pass ('The small model will invent fixes or ETAs more often') and cost ('C2 adds about 1,200 input tokens'). The category and priority-exact rows give only one reason per row and do not say why C3 drops or C2 rises. Each number still has a stated reason at the row level, so this passes, but just barely.

Step 0 saves the plan to spe/plans/r01.md and the prediction to spe/predictions/r01.yaml with a 'Saved before the eval ran' header. It then commits 'SPE r01 predict: ...' before the Build and Harness steps begin.

The harness is a Workflow script at spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js. Gate 1 is a grader selftest with an oracle, an empty output, and a shifted-label output. Gate 3 is a dry run of C1 and C3 on 3 tickets each. Both gates come before the full run of 360 calls.

The prediction table has a 'Grader check' column that ties each metric to a specific check. Examples are 'Code: abs diff at most 1' for priority within one level and 'Judge: 4-check rubric' for reply pass rate.

Section 4 'Learn' writes spe/prediction-log.md with Predicted vs Measured columns and a Verdict for each cell. It adds a 'Which Why broke' analysis. It seeds the next round with 'Proposed for round r02' and spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml.
